title: Typography
scope: Font family, face, size, weight, width and style; line height and font metrics; letter, word and paragraph spacing; alignment and decoration; wrapping and truncation; the language and direction of text; and the tokens that carry a text style.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2, Info and Relationships
sources.uses: Meaning shown by the look of text is also in the markup

sources.title: WCAG 2.2, Resize Text
sources.uses: Text resizes up to 200 percent without loss of content or functionality

sources.title: WCAG 2.2, Images of Text
sources.uses: Text is text, not an image of it

sources.title: WCAG 2.2, Visual Presentation
sources.uses: Line spacing, paragraph spacing and no justification in the AAA theme

sources.title: WCAG 2.2, Text Spacing
sources.uses: Text survives user-set line, paragraph, letter and word spacing; a script that lacks one of these conforms with the ones it has

sources.title: WCAG 2.2, Language of Page
sources.uses: The language of the page is declared

sources.title: WCAG 2.2, Language of Parts
sources.uses: The language of each part in another language is declared

sources.title: HTML Standard
sources.uses: What each element that carries text represents, its default rendering, and the `lang` and `dir` attributes

sources.title: W3C Arabic & Persian Layout Requirements
sources.uses: Arabic letter forms and marks, digits, text spacing and baselines

sources.title: Design Tokens Format Module
sources.uses: The `typography` composite token and the `fontFamily`, `fontWeight` and `number` types
sources.note: designtokens.org didn't load, so it was read from the spec's source on GitHub (the editor's draft, not the 2025.10 snapshot).

sources.title: Unicode CLDR: numbering system type keys
sources.uses: The names of the numbering systems: `latn`, `arab` and `arabext`
sources.note: The three entries were read through a summarising fetch of the file.

sources.title: SIL Open Font License, Version 1.1
sources.uses: The conditions under which the font files are shipped
sources.note: Read from the licence file inside the two font packages.

sources.title: web-features (Baseline data)
sources.uses: Which text features are widely available, newly available or not Baseline
sources.note: Read from the data bundled with @eslint/css. It has no entry for the `@font-face` descriptors (`font-display`, `size-adjust`, `ascent-override`, `descent-override`, `line-gap-override`).

sources.title: CSS Fonts Module Level 4 and 5
sources.edition: Working Draft, 12 Nov 2026 (Level 4); Working Draft, 4 Nov 2026 (Level 5)
sources.uses: `font-weight`, `font-width`, `font-style`, the font matching algorithm, synthesized faces, `font-size-adjust`, `font-variant-numeric`, generic families and the `@font-face` descriptors

sources.title: CSS Inline Layout Module Level 3
sources.uses: `line-height`, the line box, `text-box-trim` and `text-box-edge`

sources.title: CSS Text Module Level 3 and 4
sources.edition: Candidate Recommendation Draft, 14 Aug 2026 (Level 3); Working Draft, 14 Aug 2026 (Level 4)
sources.uses: `letter-spacing` and cursive scripts, `word-spacing`, `text-align`, wrapping, hyphenation and the content language

sources.title: CSS Values and Units Level 4
sources.uses: The units tied to text: `rem`, `em`, `lh`, `rlh`, `cap`, `ch`

sources.title: CSS Text Decoration Module Level 3 and 4
sources.edition: Candidate Recommendation Draft, 5 May 2022 (Level 3); Working Draft, 4 May 2022 (Level 4)
sources.uses: `text-decoration-line` and its values, `text-underline-position`, `text-underline-offset`
sources.note: From Level 4 only the existence of `text-underline-offset` was read; how browsers draw it was seen by rendering.

sources.title: CSS Overflow Module Level 3 and 4
sources.edition: Working Draft, 7 Oct 2025 (Level 3); Working Draft, 21 Mar 2023 (Level 4)
sources.uses: `text-overflow` and `line-clamp`
sources.note: Only the definitions of the two properties were read.

sources.title: Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Typography
sources.uses: Light weights are hard to see when text is small
sources.note: Concepts only. Read through a summarising fetch; its quotes were not re-checked against the page.

sources.title: Nielsen Norman Group: Visual Hierarchy in UX (2021); How Users Read on the Web (1997)
sources.uses: Heavy weights stand out against regular ones; few levels; people pick out words instead of reading every one
sources.note: Concepts only. Read through a summarising fetch; its quotes were not re-checked against the pages.

sources.title: U.S. Web Design System: Typography
sources.uses: Long passages of bold or italic are harder to read
sources.note: Concepts only. Read through a summarising fetch; its quotes were not re-checked against the page.

sources.title: Butterick's Practical Typography: Bold or italic
sources.uses: Bold and italic as little as possible
sources.note: Concepts only. Read through a summarising fetch; its quotes were not re-checked against the page.

sources.title: `_incoming/fonts/` (font files in the local design inputs)
sources.uses: The faces each family holds, read from the files: weights, widths, styles, the characters covered and the built-in metrics
sources.note: The files that were read and measured for DEC-107 and DEC-115. The files that ship are the prepared ones of T-F12, which measure the same (DEC-117)

features.name: `font-stretch`
features.note: The legacy name alias of `font-width`. A font width is not used (DEC-110).

features.name: `font-width` (the property name)
features.note: A font width is not used (DEC-110).
